entities.name: Rhonas
entities.description: The serpentine God of Strength of Amonkhet who battles the scorpion god, is killed by it, and recovers his memories of Nicol Bolas's corruption as he dies.

entities.name: The Scorpion God
entities.description: A towering scorpion-headed god, one of the original eight, corrupted by Bolas, who awakens in the Necropolis and kills Rhonas.

entities.name: The Locust God
aliases: the second of the insect gods
entities.description: A spindly, locust-like god who awakens from the Necropolis and sends a swarm of locusts to devour the Hekma.

entities.name: The Scarab God
entities.description: A god with the azure carapace of a scarab for a face who awakens from the Necropolis alongside the other two.

entities.name: Hazoret
entities.description: The spear-wielding god of Amonkhet, Rhonas's closest partner, who stands with the other gods at the Luxa.

entities.name: Oketra
entities.description: A fleet-footed god of Amonkhet who rallies her siblings to protect the mortals and recalls the prophecy that the Hekma will fall.

entities.name: Kefnet
entities.description: The proud, floating god of Amonkhet who cries out as the locusts devour the Hekma.

entities.name: Bontu
entities.description: A quiet, aloof god of Amonkhet who stands with the other gods at the Luxa.

entities.name: Nicol Bolas
entities.description: The elder dragon whom Amonkhet's mortals worship as the God-Pharaoh and whose lie Rhonas now remembers; he corrupted the gods.

entities.name: Razaketh
entities.description: A demon whose bloodspell turned the Luxa to blood and awakened the three gods; he is absent now.

entities.name: The Gods of Amonkhet
entities.description: The immortals of Amonkhet, originally eight, five of whom served the God-Pharaoh and three of whom were hidden away and corrupted.

entities.name: Rhonas's Staff-Serpent
entities.description: A living serpent into which Rhonas's staff is transformed by his last spell, torn apart by the scorpion god.

entities.name: Hour of Glory
entities.description: The promised time when the gods were to prove their worth before the God-Pharaoh, which instead brings the awakening of three forgotten gods.

entities.name: Hour of Promise
entities.description: The hour that Oketra says has begun when the locusts devour the Hekma, fulfilling the prophecy.

entities.name: The Luxa
entities.description: The river turned to blood by Razaketh that now drains through the Gate.

entities.name: Gate to the Afterlife
entities.description: The gate that opens fully at the Hours, revealing the Necropolis rather than paradise.

entities.name: The Necropolis
entities.description: The imposing building beyond the Gate housing the dead and sarcophagi that hide the three gods.

entities.name: The Hekma
entities.description: The magical barrier around Naktamun that the locusts begin to eat through.

entities.name: Naktamun
entities.description: The city of Amonkhet where the three gods enter.

entities.name: Amonkhet
entities.description: The plane whose gods were born of its mana and corrupted by the dragon.

events.summary: The story recounts the God-Pharaoh's creation myth, in which he forged five gods and set the Trials and the second sun.
events.quote: And so the great God-Pharaoh forged the gods.

events.summary: Rhonas, convinced of the myth, welcomes the Hours and goes to the Gate to greet the God-Pharaoh.
events.quote: Rhonas rejoiced, emerging from his temple and his Trial.

events.summary: All five gods gather at the bloody Luxa, but the God-Pharaoh does not arrive.
events.quote: The five stood before the crimson shores of the Luxa

events.summary: The Luxa drains through the opened Gate as the demon's spell unravels old magics.
events.quote: all that remained of the mighty Luxa was a few rivulets of red

events.summary: Three sarcophagi along the Necropolis crack open and three insect-headed gods awaken.
events.quote: three enormous figures stepped forward from their slumber, awakened by the demon's spell.

events.summary: Rhonas challenges the scorpion god, which charges him in silence.
events.quote: Without warning, the scorpion god charged toward Rhonas

events.summary: Rhonas hurls the scorpion god across the gate with a spell of vigor but it rises unharmed.
events.quote: the immortal went flying across the expanse

events.summary: Rhonas imbues his staff with poison and fells the scorpion god, which drops to its knees.
events.quote: venom powerful enough to slay most living things

events.summary: The scorpion god grapples Rhonas from behind and pierces his skull with its tail sting.
events.quote: the scorpion tail, arched over the god, piercing his own skull.

events.summary: As the poison unbinds Bolas's magic, Rhonas remembers the true history of the dragon, the corrupted gods, and the original eight.
events.quote: The great lie of the God-Pharaoh.

events.summary: Rhonas names Nicol Bolas with his dying breath and recognizes the scorpion god as one of his corrupted brothers.
events.quote: This god was once one of the original eight
as Rhonas stumbled and fell to the earth, body convulsing, then lay still.

events.summary: With his last strength, Rhonas curses the God-Pharaoh and hurls his staff, which his final spell turns into a serpent that wrestles the scorpion god.
events.quote: his final spell transforming the weapon into a living monstrous serpent

events.summary: Oketra rallies the stunned gods, and Hazoret is disturbed that Rhonas blasphemed the God-Pharaoh.
events.quote: doubt nibbled at the edges of her heart

events.summary: The locust god releases a swarm that begins eating the Hekma, and Oketra recalls the prophecy and declares the Hour of Promise has begun.
events.quote: a swarm of locusts poured forth from its hands.

events.summary: The scorpion god tears the serpent in two and advances while the other two gods enter Naktamun.
events.quote: the other two gods crossed the threshold of the gate into the city of Naktamun.

relations.note: stabbed his skull with its tail
relations.quote: Then the abomination god retracted its tail

relations.note: the scorpion god was once one of the original eight, Rhonas's brother
relations.quote: the original light and soul of his brother buried beneath vile corruption.

relations.note: siblings among the gods; he worked closest with her
relations.quote: Rhonas had worked the closest with Hazoret

relations.note: corrupted and manipulated them, erasing their origins
relations.quote: The great trespasser, slayer of mortals and corrupter of gods.

relations.note: his spell awakened the three gods
curses him as foul trespasser and destroyer in his dying shout
relations.quote: Death to the God-Pharaoh, foul trespasser and destroyer!

relations.note: his last spell transforms his staff into it
relations.quote: his final spell transforming the weapon into a living monstrous serpent
